candidate.blueprint_locator: Management of Care — scope of practice, legal responsibilities, and chain of command
candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — responding to out-of-scope assignments
candidate.educational_objective: Protect clients and nursing licensure by declining activities outside legal scope and escalating unresolved scope conflicts appropriately.

options.A: Perform the activity because supervisory authority overrides nursing law
options.B: Decline to perform the unauthorized activity and use the appropriate chain of command or regulatory resources to resolve the issue
options.C: Perform it to avoid conflict even though the activity is outside legal scope
options.D: Perform it only if another staff member agrees to observe

candidate.rationale: NCSBN's Scope of Practice Decision-Making Framework requires activities to be permitted by the nurse's education/licensure and by the nurse practice act and rules/regulations of the jurisdiction. A supervisor cannot expand legal scope by instruction. When an activity is clearly unauthorized, the nurse should not perform it and should use appropriate organizational or regulatory channels to resolve the conflict. B is correct.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Nursing activities must be permitted by the nurse's licensure and jurisdictional nurse practice act/rules; employer or supervisor direction does not replace those legal boundaries.
candidate.source_locator: Framework purpose/guidelines — determine whether an activity is permitted under education, licensure, competence, nurse practice act, and jurisdictional rules/regulations
candidate.source_organization: National Council of State Boards of Nursing (NCSBN)
candidate.stem: A supervisor directs a nurse to perform an activity that is clearly not authorized by the nurse practice act or board rules in that jurisdiction. What should the nurse do?
